Mercedes-powered cars, including championship leader **Kimi Antonelli**, have held **10 of 11 poles** this season.
**Zandvoort's Dutch Grand Prix**, the first race back from the summer break, is the first event affected by the change.

depth.background: Formula 1 introduced all-new engine ('power unit') regulations for 2026, lowering the maximum **compression ratio** — a measure of how much an engine squeezes its fuel-air mixture before ignition, which affects power and efficiency — from 18.0 to 16.0. Rivals suspected Mercedes had found a way around the spirit of that limit: compliance was only checked when the engine was cold and not running, and Mercedes was believed to be exploiting the gap between that resting measurement and how the engine actually performs once hot, during a race. Mercedes has dominated 2026 so far, with **teenage sensation Kimi Antonelli** the youngest-ever leader of the F1 drivers' championship.

stories.title: China holds military drills near Scarborough Shoal after the Philippines files a UN claim over the reef
stories.what_happened: The Philippines this week formally deposited an official nautical chart with the **United Nations**, defining the normal baselines of Scarborough Shoal and the outer limits of its 12-nautical-mile territorial sea and 24-nautical-mile contiguous zone under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. China's **People's Liberation Army Southern Theatre Command** responded on Saturday by staging joint air and naval combat drills in the waters and airspace around the shoal. In a statement, the Southern Theatre Command called the Philippine baselines **'illegal and invalid'** and said the drills were necessary to safeguard China's 'territorial sovereignty and maritime rights.' China's foreign ministry separately said Scarborough Shoal is China's 'inherent territory.' The drills came just days after the Philippines ran **joint maritime exercises with the US and Japan** in the same area.
key_points: China's military ran **joint air and naval drills** around Scarborough Shoal, days after the Philippines filed a **UN seabed claim** over the reef.
The **Philippines** submitted official nautical charts to the UN defining **territorial-sea baselines** around the shoal under international maritime law.
China's **Southern Theatre Command** called the Philippine move **'illegal and invalid'** and vowed a resolute response.
The drills follow **joint US-Japan-Philippines exercises** in the same waters days earlier.
China has held **effective control** of the shoal since a tense **2012 standoff**, despite a 2016 international tribunal ruling against its wider claims.

depth.background: Scarborough Shoal is a triangle of rocks and reefs in the South China Sea that both China (as Huangyan Dao) and the Philippines (as Bajo de Masinloc) claim as their own. China seized effective control of the shoal after a **2012 standoff** with Philippine vessels and has patrolled it with coast guard and naval ships ever since, despite a **2016 international tribunal ruling** that rejected China's broad claims to the South China Sea. The shoal sits within the Philippines' 200-nautical-mile exclusive economic zone but is more than 800km from the Chinese mainland. Tensions have flared repeatedly in recent years over Chinese coast guard vessels blocking and water-cannoning Philippine boats near the reef.

stories.title: RBI likely to hold interest rates again this week as strong growth collides with monsoon-driven inflation risk
stories.what_happened: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee meets **August 3-5**, and **SBI Research expects it to leave the repo rate unchanged** for a sixth straight meeting — even though India's GDP growth for the April-June quarter is tracking **above 7%**, stronger than expected. The reasoning: **inflation risk is rising**, not falling. Consumer price inflation is estimated to have climbed to roughly **4.4% in June**, with analysts flagging a **weak monsoon and elevated Brent crude prices** as upside risks to food and fuel costs. Separately, India's monsoon has actually **improved through July**, cutting the nationwide rainfall shortfall to **13%** from a much deeper deficit earlier in the season — a mixed signal that eases some, but not all, of the inflation worry. One forecast even sees the RBI needing **50 basis points of rate increases later in 2026** if these pressures build.
key_points: RBI's rate-setting committee meets **August 3-5**, with most analysts expecting rates to be **held steady, not cut**.
SBI Research forecasts this despite India's economy **growing faster than expected** in the April-June quarter.
**Monsoon rainfall has recovered**, cutting the nationwide shortfall to just **13%** after a weak start to the season.
Consumer inflation is estimated to have risen to around **4.4%** in June, with food-price risk still on the table.
One forecast sees **50 basis points of tightening later in 2026** even if August brings no change.

depth.background: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is India's central bank, and its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meets roughly every two months to set the **repo rate** — the rate at which it lends to commercial banks, which ripples through to loan and deposit rates across the economy. The RBI balances two goals that often pull in opposite directions: keeping **inflation** near its target (around 4%) while supporting **economic growth**. A weak or erratic **monsoon** (India's June-September rainy season) matters hugely here because it drives crop output — and therefore food prices, the biggest single component of Indian inflation.

stories.title: India's GST collections jump 15.4% to a record ₹2.11 lakh crore in July, driven by a surge in import taxes
stories.what_happened: The government released July's GST numbers on **August 1**, showing gross collections of **₹2.11 lakh crore, a 15.4% year-on-year jump**. Growth wasn't even across the board: **revenue from imports surged 28.8%** to ₹66,511 crore, while **domestic collections — from sales inside India — grew a more modest 10.1%** to ₹1.45 lakh crore. After the government paid out GST refunds, **net revenue for the month came to ₹1.81 lakh crore, up 15.8%** from a year ago. This is the **second time in the current financial year (FY27)** that monthly collections have topped the ₹2 lakh crore mark, a threshold seen as a sign of a healthy, high-consumption economy.
key_points: **Gross GST collections hit ₹2.11 lakh crore** in July, up **15.4%** from a year earlier.
**Import-linked GST revenue jumped nearly 29%** to ₹66,511 crore, far outpacing domestic growth.
**Domestic GST collections rose 10.1%** to ₹1.45 lakh crore.
After refunds, **net GST revenue rose 15.8%** to ₹1.81 lakh crore.
This is only the **second month this fiscal year** collections have crossed the ₹2 lakh crore mark.

depth.background: **GST (Goods and Services Tax)** is India's single nationwide indirect tax, charged on most goods and services sold, which replaced a patchwork of state and central taxes when it launched in 2017. The monthly GST number is one of the most closely watched **real-time gauges of India's economy** — because it's collected almost immediately after a sale happens, it shows how much buying and importing is actually going on, well before slower official GDP data arrives. The finance ministry releases this figure on the **1st of every month** for the previous month's collections.

stories.title: India opens a ₹4,000 crore credit line for Bhutan's energy projects as ties deepen
stories.what_happened: India's Foreign Secretary **Vikram Misri** concluded a two-day visit to Bhutan's capital, Thimphu, during which the two countries signed a **₹4,000 crore** concessional Line of Credit agreement between India's Export-Import Bank and Bhutan's finance ministry, earmarked for energy projects. Misri and his Bhutanese counterpart, **Dasho Pema Lektup Dorji**, co-chaired the fifth round of India-Bhutan Development Cooperation Talks, covering Bhutan's ongoing 13th Five-Year Plan. The two sides also approved **12 new projects** worth a combined ₹332 crore. Officials described the credit line as separate from and additional to India's existing ₹10,000 crore support package for Bhutan's current five-year plan, which runs from 2024 to 2029.
key_points: India signed a **₹4,000 crore concessional Line of Credit** with Bhutan, dedicated to **energy projects**.
The deal was signed during Foreign Secretary **Vikram Misri's** two-day visit to Thimphu.
The two countries also approved **12 new development projects** worth ₹332 crore.
It's **separate from** India's existing **₹10,000 crore** support package for Bhutan's current Five-Year Plan (2024-2029).
The credit line carries **below-market interest rates**, making it cheaper for Bhutan to borrow than through commercial lenders.

depth.background: Bhutan is one of India's closest strategic partners, sandwiched between India and China in the Himalayas, and India has long been its largest aid donor, trading partner, and hydropower investor. India has funded major hydropower plants in Bhutan for decades, buying the electricity back to help meet its own power needs while giving landlocked Bhutan a crucial source of export revenue. Delhi treats close ties with Thimphu as strategically important given Bhutan's position along a stretch of the disputed India-China border, including near the sensitive **Doklam plateau**, where Indian and Chinese troops faced off in 2017.

stories.title: India's August money rules kick in: a new nationwide KYC system and revised LPG prices
stories.what_happened: From August 1, **CKYC 2.0** goes live as the formally upgraded version of India's shared KYC framework, described as a move toward a 'One KYC' system. It uses real-time APIs and secure OTP-based consent so that once a customer's identity is verified with one institution, a bank, insurer, or fund house can pull the same verified record instantly using just a mobile number or PAN card — instead of asking the customer to resubmit documents each time. On the same day, IOCL, HPCL and BPCL announced their monthly revision of **domestic and commercial LPG cylinder prices** for brands like Indane, Bharat Gas and HP Gas; because the change depends on international crude and LPG benchmark prices and the rupee's exchange rate, actual new prices differ by city. The changes land alongside several other rules that reset on the 1st of the month, including revised Tatkal railway ticket booking procedures and ITR (income tax return) late-filing penalty deadlines for salaried employees.
key_points: **CKYC 2.0** — a single, shared identity-verification record for banks, insurers and mutual funds — formally launches today, August 1.
It replaces repeated paperwork with **real-time, OTP-based verification** using just your mobile number or PAN.
State-run oil firms **IOCL, HPCL and BPCL** revise domestic and commercial LPG cylinder prices today, as they do on the 1st of every month.
The changes track **international crude and LPG benchmark prices** plus the rupee's exchange rate, so the new price varies by city.
They arrive alongside a wider bundle of 1st-of-the-month changes, including new **Tatkal train-ticket booking rules** and an ITR-filing penalty deadline.

depth.background: India has long required customers to submit the same identity documents separately to every bank, insurer, and mutual fund they deal with — a process called KYC ('Know Your Customer'), meant to prevent fraud and money laundering. A **Central KYC Registry (CKYC)**, run by an RBI/SEBI/IRDAI-backed body, already lets institutions share a customer's verified records, but the system has been clunky. LPG (cooking gas) cylinder prices, meanwhile, are reviewed and adjusted every month by India's state oil marketing companies based on global fuel costs — a routine but closely watched process because gas costs affect nearly every household budget.

stories.title: Bangladesh's envoy to India says Dhaka 'will not become a playground' for China or Pakistan against Indian interests
stories.what_happened: In an interview with **Deccan Chronicle**, Bangladesh's high commissioner to India, **Muhammad Riaz Hamidullah**, sought to calm Indian unease over Dhaka's outreach to Beijing and Islamabad, saying Bangladeshi soil **'will never be used against Indian interests by anyone'** and that India remains Bangladesh's **predominant trading partner**. He acknowledged that the 2024 uprising and Bangladesh's participation in China's **Belt and Road Initiative** had created an impression of drift between the two neighbours, but argued the China relationship itself was **not new**. Hamidullah also raised **irregular migration**, saying Bangladesh is ready to take back any of its nationals confirmed to have entered India illegally, while asking India to also address the **trafficking networks** that enable such migration, and he invited **Indian universities, tech, and agritech firms** to invest in Bangladesh. The interview surfaced around the same time India's outgoing envoy to Dhaka separately said relations would move **'constructively'** once Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman **visits India** — an invitation from PM Modi that Dhaka has said it is still **reviewing**.
key_points: Bangladesh's high commissioner **Muhammad Riaz Hamidullah** said Dhaka is mindful of India's security concerns and **'will not become a playground for anyone else.'**
The reassurance comes as Bangladesh's new **BNP government under PM Tarique Rahman**, elected in **February 2026**, deepens engagement with **China**, including Belt-and-Road-linked projects.
Hamidullah called Dhaka's relationship with China **'not new'** and instead pitched for **more Indian investment**, saying Indian firms were ceding ground to European companies in Bangladesh.

The remarks land alongside a **separate reassurance from India's outgoing envoy** that ties will move forward **'constructively'** once PM Rahman visits India — an invitation Dhaka is still **reviewing**.

Relations have been strained since the **2024 uprising** that ousted Sheikh Hasina, who has since taken shelter in India, with India summoning Bangladesh's envoy as recently as **late 2025** over security concerns.

depth.background: India-Bangladesh ties were close under Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government but **fractured after a mass uprising forced her from power in August 2024**; she has lived in India ever since, and Dhaka has sought her return to face charges, an unresolved sore point. An **interim government led by Muhammad Yunus** ran Bangladesh until a general election on **February 12, 2026**, which the **Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)** won in a landslide, installing **Tarique Rahman as prime minister** on February 17. Since taking office, Rahman's government has pursued a self-described **'Bangladesh first'** foreign policy — engaging China and, more cautiously, Pakistan — which has fed Indian anxiety about a neighbour drifting into **Beijing's orbit**, a concern India has long framed using the idea of a Chinese **'String of Pearls'** of influence around it. Ties hit a low point in late 2025 when India summoned Bangladesh's high commissioner over security concerns.

stories.title: Table-topping Jaffna Kings, already through to the playoffs, face bottom-placed Dambulla Sixers today as the Lanka Premier League's group stage wraps up
stories.what_happened: Jaffna Kings have been the form team of the tournament, winning five of seven games to top the table and already banking a playoff berth, with **Towhid Hridoy** — signed only as a late replacement — playing a key role in two rapid cameos since joining. Dambulla Sixers, by contrast, have won just once in six games and sit at the bottom, having lost their last three matches in a row, including a defeat to Colombo Kaps earlier this week. Ahead of today's meeting, Dambulla brought in Zimbabwe all-rounder **Sikandar Raza** as an injury replacement, while other franchises reshuffled too: Galle Gallants (currently top of the table on the back of a strong campaign) lost Australian batter Chris Lynn to injury and let Mehidy Hasan Miraz depart early, bringing in Australia's Thomas Rogers as cover. With the playoffs — an Eliminator and Qualifier 1 on August 5, Qualifier 2 on August 7 and the final on August 8, all at the Premadasa Stadium in Colombo — now just days away, today's result and net run rate could still shape who finishes where.
key_points: **Jaffna Kings** sit top of the 2026 Lanka Premier League table with **5 wins from 7 games (10 points)** and have already secured a **playoff spot**.
**Dambulla Sixers** are bottom of the table, having won just once in six games, and must beat Jaffna today and hope other results fall their way to have any hope of survival.

Bangladesh batter **Towhid Hridoy**, brought in only after teammate Taskin Ahmed withdrew, has hit **35 off 21 and 31 off 8** in his first two Jaffna innings — form that helped drag the team off the bottom of the table.
Multiple franchises made **late squad changes** this week: Dambulla added Zimbabwe's **Sikandar Raza**, while Galle Gallants lost **Chris Lynn** (injury) and **Mehidy Hasan Miraz** (early departure).
The **LPL playoffs** begin August 5 at the R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo, with the final set for August 8.

depth.background: The **Lanka Premier League (LPL)** is Sri Lanka Cricket's flagship T20 franchise tournament, a shop window that mixes international stars with young Sri Lankan talent and returned this year after a two-year hiatus, with the 2026 season opening on July 17. Six franchises play a round-robin, and the **top four** advance to a knockout stage. Because overseas players in T20 leagues are often on short-term deals tied to their national team's schedule, squads change constantly mid-tournament — as seen this week with several franchises swapping players in and out just before the final round-robin fixtures. Today's Dambulla vs Jaffna match at **Pallekele International Cricket Stadium** is effectively the last item of unfinished business before the playoff picture is set.

stories.title: India's judo team wins a fourth Commonwealth Games medal as Unnati Sharma battles to bronze in Glasgow
stories.what_happened: On day 9 of the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, Unnati Sharma won bronze in the women's -63kg judo category, taking India's judo medal tally at these Games to four. She began with an ippon victory over Eswatini's Lamulela Magagula in the round of 16, then narrowly beat New Zealand's Qona Christie by waza-ari in the quarter-finals to reach the last four. In the semi-final she lost by ippon to Australia's Saya Middleton, who went on to win silver, dropping Sharma into the bronze-medal playoff. She won that decisively, defeating South Africa's Skye Knoester by ippon in just **one minute and seven seconds**. Two teammates, Karanjit Singh Maan (men's -90kg) and Harsh Tokas (men's -81kg), reached their own bronze-medal contests today but both lost, ending their medal hopes.
key_points: Unnati Sharma wins **bronze in the women's -63kg** category, India's **fourth judo medal** of the 2026 Games.
She opened with an **ippon win** over Eswatini's Lamulela Magagula, then edged New Zealand's Qona Christie in the quarter-finals.
A semi-final loss to eventual silver medallist **Saya Middleton** of Australia sent her into the bronze playoff.
She sealed bronze with an **ippon in just 1:07 minutes** over South Africa's Skye Knoester.
Teammates **Karanjit Singh Maan** and **Harsh Tokas** both fell just short of the podium in their own weight categories today.

depth.background: Judo has historically been a minor medal source for India at the Commonwealth Games, with the contingent traditionally built around athletics, wrestling and boxing. That changed at Glasgow 2026: judokas **Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh** had already won India's first-ever Commonwealth Games judo golds earlier in the Games. Unnati Sharma, competing in the women's -63kg category, was part of a young judo squad hoping to build on that breakthrough. In judo scoring, a full point (ippon) wins a bout outright, while lesser scores (waza-ari) can add up — meaning matches can turn in seconds.
